newsitem.title: UK: IGC trims E.Europe wheat crop estimates after rain.
newsitem.headline: IGC trims E.Europe wheat crop estimates after rain.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday reduced its estimates for Czech, Slovak, Polish and Romanian wheat crops as a result of recent rains and flooding in the region.

The rain had significant impact on Romania, the IGC said in its latest Grains Market Report. Romania's estimated crop was cut to 7.1 million tonnes compared with the previous estimate of 7.8 million. But "the outturn will still be a huge improvement on last year's poor crop of 3.2 million tonnes," it said.

The IGC also revised its estimate for the 1997 Czech wheat crop down to 3.3 million tonnes compared with the previous 3.7 million. 1996 output was 3.7 million. Heavy rainfall and floods affected about 130,000 hectares of agricultural land.

For Poland, hit by severe floods in southern and southwestern regions, the crop was cut by 300,000 tonnes to 7.9 million, compared with 1996's 8.5 million. The estimate for the Slovak harvest was reduced by 200,000 tonnes to 1.7 million.

Hungary's harvest has been delayed by heavy rain over the past two weeks, the IGC said. It raised its production estimate by 100,000 tonnes to 5.1 million but expressed concern over quality. "Recent reports show some deterioration due to excessive moisture," it said.
Wet weather has also delayed the harvest in Croatia. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
